title.value: EpiK-Eval: Evaluation for Language Models as Epistemic Models
title.justification: The title was directly extracted from the paper, indicating the introduction of a benchmark tailored to evaluate language models.
title.quote: This paper presents the first study examining the capability of LLMs to effectively combine such information within their parameter space. We introduce EpiK-Eval, a novel question-answering benchmark tailored to evaluate LLMs’ proficiency in formulating a coherent and consistent knowledge representation from segmented narratives.

extractions.description: The paper introduces EpiK-Eval, a novel question-answering benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) in their ability to consolidate knowledge from segmented narratives. This assessment aims to determine if LLMs can maintain a coherent and consistent knowledge state, an essential trait for effective reasoning and applications. Evaluations show significant weaknesses in LLMs' ability to consolidate knowledge, suggesting a need for refining training objectives to enhance their reasoning capabilities.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on evaluating the internal capabilities of language models and does not discuss any direct applications, impacts, or contributions to eco-responsible AI categories.
primary_category.quote: Despite their growing prevalence, their capacity to consolidate knowledge from different training documents—a crucial ability in numerous applications—remains unexplored.

secondary_categories.justification: The content of the paper is focused on theoretical and methodological advancements in AI without a connection to eco-responsible or environmental aspects.
secondary_categories.quote: Thus far, assessing parametric knowledge representations has garnered interest on two ends of a spectrum.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit any specific eco-responsible sub-category as it primarily addresses methodological improvements in AI.
primary_sub_category.quote: To this end, we propose the novel Epistemic Knowledge Evaluation (EpiK-Eval) benchmark, to evaluate this ability to leverage such a consolidated knowledge state.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Since the paper does not discuss applications related to environmental or sustainable practices, no secondary sub-categories are applicable.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We introduce EpiK-Eval, a novel question-answering benchmark tailored to evaluate LLMs’ proficiency in formulating a coherent and consistent knowledge representation from segmented narratives.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on developing a benchmark to assess language models' knowledge consolidation, which is a methodological advancement rather than an eco-responsible application.
new_primary_category.quote: We introduce EpiK-Eval, a novel question-answering benchmark tailored to evaluate LLMs’ proficiency in formulating a coherent and consistent knowledge representation from segmented narratives.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: EpiK-Eval is specifically designed to evaluate how language models consolidate and represent knowledge, which aligns with this proposed sub-category.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: By highlighting current limitations and opportunities for improving LMs, these results delineate paths for future research, hopefully enabling the growth of language models beyond simple knowledge bases.
